decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 1% to 1.25%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: The fundamentals of the U.S. economy remain strong.

changes.quote: However, the coronavirus poses evolving risks to economic activity.

changes.quote: In light of these risks and in support of achieving its maximum employment and price stability goals, the Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point, to 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of these risks and in support of achieving its maximum employment and price stability goals, the Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point, to 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
However, the coronavirus poses evolving risks to economic activity.
The Committee is closely monitoring developments and their implications for the economic outlook and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 14.87% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.02% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.49% would fall by about $13.35 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 190k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.6% over the past year (January 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -13 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -2.81%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.27% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 23%, cut 77%, hike 0%.
